subject: Re: Serving strategy & migration constraints for MedSolutions
messages:
From: Erin Coleman <erin@medsolutions.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Serving strategy discussion follow-up

Thanks again for the demo earlier. As discussed, we need to settle on the serving approach before procurement can move forward. High level notes from our side: we currently run a mix of an external LLM API (MacroAI) for low-risk features and a self-hosted legacy GPU cluster for higher-volume batch tasks. Our security team prefers VPC/private deployment for PHI workflows, but product wants the flexibility of hosted during the pilot.

Two immediate asks:
- Can Redwood support a hybrid approach during POC (hosted for dev + dedicated reserved pool for production)?
- What does migration look like for our self-hosted embeddings and legacy KV cache (we have >2TB of cached tensors)?

I attached our POC requirements spreadsheet and a rough network diagram.

Cheers,
Erin Coleman
Head of Platform Engineering
MedSolutions

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Erin Coleman <erin@medsolutions.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Serving strategy discussion follow-up

Erin — thanks for the clear summary and the files, they were helpful. Short answers up front: yes, we can run a hybrid POC (hosted for dev + Dedicated reserved pool for production-like throughput) and we support VPC/private deployment for regulated workloads. Migration of cached KV tensors is feasible but depends on the storage format and checkpointing cadence — we'd like to see an export sample.

Next steps I propose:
1) Tech sync (30–45 min) with your infra lead to walk the network diagram and VPC/KMS constraints.
2) Confirmation of target SLOs (p95 latency target, tokens/sec, concurrency) so we size Dedicated.
3) Short migration analysis: we will validate embedding vector formats and a plan to warm the cache to avoid cold-start token spikes.

Jonas — can you join the tech sync and own the migration checklist? I'll include Ben for procurement cadence and SOW redlines.

Best,
Grace O'Connor

grace_oconnor@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Serving strategy discussion follow-up

Erin, Grace — thanks, jumping in with a few technical clarifications from infra/serving side: 
- Hybrid POC pattern we recommend: hosted API (dev) -> Dedicated reserved pool (staging/prod) -> Private VPC for regulated PHI lanes. That allows you to validate prompts and model variants without early procurement lock-in.
- Migration notes: we've onboarded customers migrating from MacroAI and self-hosted TF/PyTorch clusters. Typical blockers are: tokenization model mismatch, embedding dimension differences, KV cache serialization, and network egress rules for large cache warming.

Questions for your infra team prior to the tech sync:
1) Which KMS provider are you using (AWS KMS, HashiCorp Vault, HSM)?
2) Are there egress restrictions from your VPC that would block outbound pulls for container images or model shards?
3) Is your legacy cache stored as raw tensors or as sharded LMKV snapshots?

I'll draft a migration checklist after the call outlining: export sample, tokenization mapping test, cache warm strategy (bulk warm vs on-demand warm), and rollback thresholds.

— Jonas
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Erin Coleman <erin@medsolutions.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@medsolutions.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Serving strategy discussion follow-up

Thanks Jonas — answers inline: 
- KMS: AWS KMS for now; we may evaluate external HSM for later.
- Egress: production VPC has strict egress via proxy; we can allow specific endpoints but need to maintain audit logs.
- Cache: legacy cache is stored as sharded LMKV snapshots (custom serializer). We can export a small shard for testing.

Tech sync availability: Mon 10/4 09:00–12:00 PT or Tue 10/5 13:00–16:00 PT.

Also, procurement wants an estimate of the monthly committed throughput and an example SOW with milestones (POC, staging run, production handoff). Can Redwood provide a draft SOW and a ballpark committed GPU pool (e.g., equivalent v100/gpu-days or p4d slots)?

Regards,
Erin

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Erin Coleman <erin@medsolutions.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Serving strategy & migration constraints for MedSolutions

Erin — looping in procurement/solutions thread. Quick answers while we set the tech sync: 
- We'll share a draft SOW and a committed-capacity estimate by EOD Mon (10/4). The draft will include: POC acceptance criteria, staging throughput test, cache-warming milestone, security verification (VPC/KMS), and production cutover checklist.
- Ballpark committed capacity: for the workload you described (high-volume embeddings + mid-size generation), expect an initial reserved pool equivalent to ~8 p4d slots or 48 V100-equivalent GPU-days/month. We'll refine after we get your p95 latency and qps targets.
- Regarding migration from MacroAI: we can coordinate a phased traffic-shift with canary routing; we support dual-writing embeddings during transition to avoid data loss.

Next concrete items:
1) Confirm tech sync time (Jonas + Grace + Erin + Raj).
2) Erin to upload a sample LMKV shard and a 5–10 example prompt set for tokenization checks.
3) Redwood to produce SOW draft and initial capacity estimate (due 10/4 EOD).

Thanks — Ben
